title: Protocol for the DHA Oxford Learning And Behaviour Study
author: Paul Montgomery
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.k8kczuw

steps.title: Screen Participants for Eligibility
steps.instruction: Identify potential participants from year groups 3, 4, and 5 who are in the lowest quintile for literacy based on Key Stage 1 assessments at age 7.

substeps.instruction: Verify with teachers that the child's reading is still a cause for concern and that they have no other significant learning difficulties.
Confirm the child has no major learning disabilities or medical disorders.
Ensure the child's first language is English.
Exclude children taking medications affecting behavior/learning, those already taking omega-3 supplements, or those eating fish more than twice per week.

steps.title: Obtain Informed Consent
steps.instruction: Secure written proxy consent from parents/caregivers and verbal assent from the children.

substeps.instruction: Send invitation letters and detailed participant information to parents via the school.
Conduct telephone calls, home visits, or school meetings to discuss the study and answer questions.

steps.title: Conduct Baseline Assessments
steps.instruction: Perform a series of baseline measures to confirm eligibility and establish a starting point.

substeps.instruction: Administer the BAS 3 word reading test; only children in the bottom 20th centile are invited to the RCT.
Collect teacher ratings using the Conners Teacher Ratings (CTRS-L) and record school attendance over the previous term.
Collect parent ratings using Conners Parent Ratings (CPRS-L), a health questionnaire, and demographics via Freepost mail.
Administer the BAS II Recall of Digits (working memory) test to the child.
Perform an optional fingerprick blood sample to assess fatty acid status (DHA Omega-3, AA, and EPA Omega-3).

steps.title: Randomize Participants
steps.instruction: Allocate eligible children to either the active DHA Omega-3 group or the placebo group using a computer-generated sequence with a minimization algorithm for sex and school balance.

steps.title: Administer Study Treatment
steps.instruction: Provide the allocated supplement daily for 16 weeks.

substeps.instruction: Dose: 3 x 500 mg capsules per day (total 600 mg DHA Omega-3 as a triglyceride for the active group; corn/soy oil for the placebo group).
Administration: Delivered by teachers Monday–Friday and by parents/caregivers on weekends and school holidays.
Storage: Use coded bottles with 2-part labels (inner portion for protocol/allocation details, outer tear-off portion for initials).

steps.title: Perform Bi-weekly Monitoring
steps.instruction: Contact parents via telephone every fortnight to track health and attendance.

substeps.instruction: Log any school absences due to illness (e.g., upper/lower respiratory, ear infections, vomiting, diarrhea, rash, ectopy, food allergy, asthma, fever, lower GI/gastritis).
Inquire about any adverse events.

steps.title: Conduct Post-Intervention Assessments
steps.instruction: Perform final evaluations at Day 112 (+/- 2 days) to measure the impact of the intervention.

substeps.instruction: Administer teacher ratings (CTRS-L) and record attendance over the past term.
Administer child tests: Reading test age and working memory digit span test.
Perform a fingerprick blood sample to assess compliance and fatty acid status.
Collect parent ratings (CPRS-L), health questionnaire, and the Barkley Side Effects Rating Scale (SERS) via Freepost mail.
Administer a 'Prediction of treatment group' test to verify blinding.

steps.title: Verify Compliance and Close Study
steps.instruction: Assess adherence to the treatment regimen and conclude participation.

substeps.instruction: Collect all unused supplements and perform a pill count.
Provide all participants with a 3-month supply of Life’s DHA as a token of thanks.
